title: Present continuous and present simple 2
subtitle: She goes up to this man ... / He's always offering to help
summary: Use present tenses for stories, commentaries, headlines and repeated behaviour that is typical of someone.

lesson.heading: Stories and jokes
lesson.text: In informal spoken English we often tell a story or a joke in the present, to make it feel as if the events are happening now. The main events come in sequence in the present simple; longer background events are in the present continuous.

examples.text: She **goes** up to this man and **looks** straight into his eyes. He**'s not wearing** his glasses, and he **doesn't recognise** her ...
This man**'s playing** golf when a kangaroo **bounds** up to him, **grabs** his club and **hits** his ball about half a mile ...

lesson.heading: Highlighting one event
lesson.text: In a narrative or anecdote the present simple can be used to highlight a single event, often after past tenses and with a phrase such as *suddenly* or *all of a sudden*.

examples.text: I was sitting in the park, reading a newspaper, when all of a sudden this dog **jumps** at me.

lesson.heading: Live commentary
lesson.text: In live commentaries - on sports events, for example - the report happens at the same time as the action, so we use the present simple for the moves and the present continuous for the longer picture.

examples.text: King **serves** to the left-hand court and Adams **makes** a wonderful return. She**'s playing** magnificent tennis in this match ...

lesson.heading: Introducing news you have heard or read
lesson.text: We use the present simple in phrases such as **It says here, I hear, I gather, I see, I understand, They say, (Someone) says, (Someone) tells me** to introduce news that we have heard, read, seen or been told.

examples.text: **Sophia tells me** you're thinking of emigrating.
Professor Hendriks is at the conference and **I hear** she's an excellent speaker.

lesson.note: Past tenses are also possible here: It said here ..., I heard ...

lesson.heading: Headlines, books and films
lesson.text: News headlines use the present simple for events that have recently happened. We also use it for the contents of books, films and newspapers.

examples.text: SECOND QUAKE **HITS** JAPAN / FIRE **BREAKS** OUT IN HOTEL ROOM / SCIENTISTS **FIND** ICE ON THE MOON / FOREIGN MINISTER **RESIGNS**
Thompson **gives** a list of the largest European companies in Chapter 6.
At the beginning of the book, three men **find** $4 million in a crashed plane.
In the film, Loni Baranski **takes** the role of a private detective.

lesson.heading: always, constantly, continually, forever
lesson.text: The present continuous with these adverbs emphasises that something is done so often that it is characteristic of a person, group or thing. It often shows disapproval.

examples.text: *A:* I think I'll stay here after all. *B:* You**'re constantly changing** your mind.
Jacob is a really kind person. He**'s always offering** to help me with my work.

lesson.note: The past continuous works the same way: Was Olivia always asking you for money, too?

lesson.heading: What you are normally doing at a certain time
lesson.text: We can use the present continuous to describe something we regularly do at a particular time of day.

examples.text: At eight o'clock I**'m** usually **driving** to work, so phone me on my mobile.
Seven o'clock is a bit early. We**'re** generally **eating** then.

lesson.text: In a spoken story, ask whether the verb pushes the story forward (present simple) or paints the scene it happens in (present continuous).

exercises.prompt: Rodriguez passes to Messi who ___ just over the bar.
exercises.explanation: A single move in a live commentary: present simple.

exercises.prompt: Rodriguez passes to Messi who shoots just over the bar. Barcelona ___ much more in this half ...
exercises.explanation: The longer picture behind the individual moves takes the present continuous.

exercises.statement: SCIENTISTS FIND ICE ON THE MOON
exercises.explanation: Correct. News headlines use the present simple for events that have recently happened.

exercises.prompt: A man ___ home late one night after the office Christmas party.
exercises.explanation: A main event in a spoken story: present simple.

exercises.prompt: A man arrives home late one night after the office Christmas party. His wife ___ for him, and she says to him ...
exercises.explanation: Waiting is the longer background situation, so the present continuous is used.

exercises.prompt: Match each remark with the reply that complains about what the other person always does.

pairs.right: *B:* You're always complaining about my handwriting.
*B:* You're forever asking me for money.

pairs.left: *A:* That was a dangerous thing to do.
*A:* I think I'll stay here after all.
*A:* I had a bad day at the office again.
pairs.right: *B:* You're forever moaning about your work.

exercises.prompt: Finish the anecdote: 'I was sitting in the park, reading a newspaper, when ...'
exercises.answer: all of a sudden this dog jumps at me
exercises.explanation: The present simple after a past tense, with all of a sudden, highlights the event.

exercises.prompt: I went to a concert yesterday in the Town Hall. In the middle of it, while the orchestra ___, this man suddenly stands on his seat and starts to conduct them.
exercises.explanation: The orchestra's playing is the background to the highlighted events, so present continuous.

exercises.prompt: Gielman ___ Henry V in the latest production at the Royal Theatre.
exercises.explanation: We use the present simple to describe the contents of a book, a film or a production.

exercises.prompt: *Headline:* Vegecorp to sack 1,000 workers. -- ___ Vegecorp are going to sack a thousand workers.
exercises.explanation: The present simple in I gather / I hear / I understand introduces news you have read or been told.

exercises.prompt: *Ed:* Did you hear that Bruno's crashed his car again? -- ___ Bruno's crashed his car again.
exercises.explanation: (Someone) tells me is another present simple phrase for reporting news.

exercises.prompt: In these spoken stories and commentaries, which tense does each part need?
categories: Present simple - a main event in the sequence
Present continuous - a longer background event
